claim.pdf_says: The two trailing bracketed lines of PERFORM Format 3 are printed as `[ WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION  imperative-statement-3 ]` and `[ WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-4 ]`. Verified at 900 dpi: on the OTHER line an underline runs under WHEN and under OTHER; on the COMMON line the underline runs under COMMON only — the word WHEN on the `WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION` line has NO underline beneath it. This is an inconsistency in the printed standard itself, since WHEN is required in both alternatives.
claim.markdown_says: Figure note: "`PERFORM`, `LOCATION`, `WHEN`, `EXCEPTION`, `INPUT`, `OUTPUT`, `IO`, `EXTEND`, `FILE`, `OTHER`, `COMMON`, `FINALLY`, and `END-PERFORM` are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `WITH` is printed without an underline, as is the second `EXCEPTION` in each of the `WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION` / `WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION` lines."
claim.why_it_matters: The note is otherwise a careful, verified record of this figure's typography — it even captures the un-underlined second EXCEPTION — but it flattens `WHEN` to "underlined" and so silently loses an ISO printing defect that a later reader re-checking the page will trip over and may mistake for a transcription error. Project practice is to record ISO's own defects rather than normalize them away. No COBOL semantics change: WHEN is required in the COMMON alternative regardless.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed independently, twice, by two methods; every refutation avenue was tried and failed.

(1) VISUAL, 900 dpi clip render of the band (fitz clip Rect(60,618,320,652), written to E:/Temp/specrecon/v712/zoom_when_900.png). At that magnification the two lines read unambiguously: on `[ WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION imperative-statement-3 ]` there are two short rules, one under WHEN and one under OTHER; on `[ WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-4 ]` there is exactly one rule and it sits under COMMON. The space beneath WHEN on the COMMON line is blank.

(2) VECTOR GEOMETRY, which is decisive and not subject to raster/anti-alias judgement. The underlines in this PDF are thin filled rects (height 0.467 pt). Enumerating page.get_drawings() and coalescing abutting rects yields, for the three bracketed lines:
      y=634.55  x  75.36.. 98.93  (w 23.58)   <- OTHER line, rule 1
      y=634.55  x 103.60..129.28  (w 25.68)   <- OTHER line, rule 2
      y=648.79  x 103.60..138.62  (w 35.02)   <- COMMON line, ONLY rule
      y=662.80  x  75.36..107.11  (w 31.75)   <- FINALLY line
The text layer is glyph-obfuscated (uppercase = codepoint+61, lowercase = codepoint-34), but bounding boxes are intact. Decoding and matching word extents against the rules gives:
      [ WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION imperative-statement-3 ]
         WHEN   x  74.58.. 99.63  UNDERLINED (rule 75.36..98.93, 94% cover)
         OTHER  x 102.78..130.14  UNDERLINED (rule 103.60..129.28, 94% cover)
         EXCEPTION x 132.68..177.30  plain
      [ WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-4 ]
         WHEN   x  74.57.. 99.62  NO RULE ANYWHERE NEAR IT
         COMMON x 102.77..139.33  UNDERLINED (rule 103.60..138.62, 96% cover)
         EXCEPTION x 141.87..186.48  plain
The two WHENs occupy essentially identical x-extents (74.58..99.63 vs 74.57..99.62), so this is not a measurement or alignment artefact: a rule exists at that x on one line and simply does not exist on the other.

DETECTOR VALIDATED, not assumed. Re-running with a wider y-band flipped END-PERFORM from 'plain' to UNDERLINED (rule y=677.04, x 69.75..126.24) — its rule had merely fallen outside the first band. All three bracketed lines' rules (634.55 / 648.79 / 662.80) were comfortably inside the original band, so the 'plain' verdict on the COMMON-line WHEN is a real absence, not band clipping.

THIRD OCCURRENCE, for precision: Format 3 prints WHEN three times. The brace-group WHEN at y 542.61..552.87 IS underlined (rule y=553.55, x 76.99..100.57, width 23.58 — identical width to the OTHER-line WHEN rule, 23.58). So two of the three WHENs carry a rule and exactly one, on the `WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION` line, does not.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS, all failed:
  - Misquote? No. The markdown figure note is reproduced verbatim from specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29095; the PDF line text decodes exactly as claimed, including the double space after EXCEPTION on the OTHER line.
  - Already recorded elsewhere? No. The companion note at line 29096 covers only the exception-name-1/-2 brace lines. Grepping for 'not underlined' / 'without an underline' shows the spec-wide figure-note convention is to enumerate underlined and non-underlined words exhaustively (see lines 3964, 9457, 14845, 14853, 15490, ...), so this note presents itself as a complete typographic record — and is wrong on one word.
  - Mere formatting, therefore ignorable? No. In COBOL general formats underlining is load-bearing notation, not decoration: ISO 1989:2023 states that uppercase words that are NOT underlined are optional words (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 2641 and 5805). Read literally, the printed page makes WHEN optional in the COMMON alternative.
  - Is it therefore a semantic difference rather than a printing defect? No — the claim's reading is right. General rules 17, 18 and 19 all say 'if WHEN COMMON is specified', and every annex example writes `WHEN COMMON` (lines 45192, 45229). WHEN is required in both alternatives, so the missing rule is a defect in ISO's own typesetting.

The claim is accurate as written, including its severity (cosmetic — the transcription loses a typographic fact about the printed page, and no COBOL semantics change).
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed; one detail worth adding for precision. On page 712 the PERFORM Format 3 diagram prints WHEN three times: in the brace group (underlined — rule y=553.55, x 76.99..100.57), on the `[ WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION imperative-statement-3 ]` line (underlined — rule y=634.55, x 75.36..98.93), and on the `[ WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-4 ]` line, where there is NO underline: the only rule on that line is y=648.79, x 103.60..138.62, under COMMON. Confirmed both visually at 900 dpi and by the PDF's underline rects (thin filled rects, height 0.467 pt) matched against decoded word bounding boxes; the two WHENs sit at effectively identical x-extents (74.58..99.63 and 74.57..99.62), so the absence is real and not an alignment artefact. This is a defect in ISO's printing, not a semantic signal — GRs 17/18/19 all read 'if WHEN COMMON is specified' and the annex examples write `WHEN COMMON`, so WHEN is required in both alternatives. Suggested repair to the figure note at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29095: keep WHEN in the underlined list but append the exception, e.g. "...; `WITH` is printed without an underline, as is the second `EXCEPTION` in each of the `WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION` / `WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION` lines. Note also that `WHEN` is underlined in the brace group and on the `WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION` line but is printed WITHOUT an underline on the `WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION` line — an inconsistency in the printed standard, since WHEN is required there too (general rules 17 to 19 all read 'if WHEN COMMON is specified')."
